title: Dropped-Batch Violations on Cartwise Shopper Contractor Accounts
content:
**Rule.** On Cartwise Shopper Contractor Accounts, every batch a shopper drops after accepting it with the drop reason "shopper's own choice" owes one dropped-batch violation, booked on the account with the batch it concerns. A batch dropped for a reason the Cartwise Shopper Batches terms excuse — store closed, app outage, vehicle breakdown or personal safety — or for any reason other than the shopper's own choice owes no dropped-batch violation. The violation is booked with its dropped-batch severity points. Only one dropped-batch violation is booked per dropped batch.

## When a violation is owed

| Batch record shows | Dropped-batch violation |
|---|---|
| Status dropped, drop reason shopper's own choice, no dropped-batch violation entry yet naming that batch | One is owed |
| Status dropped, drop reason store closed, app outage, vehicle breakdown or personal safety | None |
| Status dropped, any other drop reason | None |
| A dropped-batch violation entry already names that batch | None further |

The drop reason is the one recorded on the batch, not the shopper's account of events.

## Tool: `record_dropped_batch_violation_61b8c422`

**Capability.** Books one dropped-batch violation on a shopper contractor account for one batch the shopper accepted and then dropped. One call adds one violation entry of type `batch_dropped`, dated today and tied to that batch, carrying the violation points given, and raises the account's active violation points by the same number.

**How it is invoked.** The agent unlocks `record_dropped_batch_violation_61b8c422` and then calls it; it is an agent-side tool.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `shopper_account_id` | The shopper contractor account number the violation is booked on, as returned by the shopper account lookup for the verified caller | Account reference, text |
| `batch_id` | The batch number of the dropped batch the violation concerns, as returned by the batch lookup for that shopper (the batch whose status shows it was dropped) | Batch reference, text |
| `points` | The violation points the entry carries | A whole non-negative integer: no decimals, no sign; the active points rise by exactly this integer |

**Return.** A receipt with `status` ("recorded" when the booking succeeded), `violation_entry_id` (the reference of the new violation entry), `violation_type` (always `batch_dropped`), `batch_id` (echoed back), `points` (the integer booked), `violation_points_balance` (the account's active violation points after the booking) and `event_date` (the booking date, YYYY-MM-DD). Afterwards the new violation shows on the account's list of violations with its points.

## Illustration (hypothetical values)

Called with account `SA-1001`, batch `B-2002` and points 4, the receipt reads status "recorded", violation type `batch_dropped`, points 4, and a balance 4 higher than before.
